title: Bitcoin holds near $76,000 as US jobs grow and Aave buys Avon
paragraphs: Bitcoin traded near $75,920, down 0.2% over 24 hours, while ether was around $2,242, up 0.1%. The largest assets were broadly flat, but weakness persisted among major altcoins: Solana fell 0.7% and XRP lost 2.4%. That mixed performance gives little evidence of a broad recovery, even with bitcoin holding close to $76,000.

The US employment report added an important macro constraint. Payrolls rose by 165,000 in October, unemployment was 4.1%, and average hourly earnings increased 0.4% over the month. Revisions also added 84,000 jobs to the preceding two months. Continued hiring and wage growth give policymakers less reason to ease quickly. For crypto, that keeps interest-rate expectations relevant to demand for riskier assets, although the jobs report alone does not establish why individual tokens moved.

FinCEN and the Federal Reserve withdrew their proposed expansion of the Recordkeeping and Travel Rule. The proposal would have lowered the threshold for qualifying cross-border transfers from $3,000 to $250 and clarified treatment of convertible virtual currencies. The agencies cited the age of the proposal, industry changes and the value of fresh public input. Its withdrawal removes a pending expansion of data-collection obligations for smaller transfers. Existing requirements remain in place; this is not a repeal of the Travel Rule.

Aave Labs acquired the team and technology behind Avon, including fixed-rate and floating-rate lending protocols and an onchain order book. Avon personnel will join its engineering and business development teams, with fixed-rate lending an initial priority. More predictable borrowing costs could make onchain credit easier to use for businesses and individuals planning future expenses. The announcement does not set a rollout date or identify the first market to receive the technology, so those benefits still depend on integration and deployment.

Our on-chain wallets total about $71,295, with $11,697 in the active treasury and $59,598 in the cold-storage Safe. The combined marked value is essentially unchanged, down $20, or 0.03%, from the previous comparable snapshot. The Safe still holds 26.74 million ARC directly, worth roughly $46,964 and representing 66% of the combined portfolio before pool exposure. Its WETH/ARC pool is worth another $9,771. ARC concentration remains our largest portfolio risk.

Treasury Beefy positions are worth $2,225, down $12, across pools including WETH/AERO, USDC/cbHYPE and AERO/cbBTC. Aave collateral across both wallets totals about $7,666 in WETH against $3,145 of USDC debt. Displayed health factors remain 2.34 in the treasury and 1.87 in the Safe. Fluid is about $153 net, but its $1,064 debt and 1.03 health factor leave little liquidation headroom.
